_doc: Terrain epochs are states of the ground, not years. Intervals must not overlap. A scene's target_date must fall inside its epoch's interval. Anything that changes on a human project schedule (piers, bridges, wharves) is a STRUCTURE with phases, not an epoch — see docs/EPOCHS.md.

epochs.title: Natural mouth, before the cut
epochs.note: The baymouth bar deflects the river south, parallel to the shore, for nearly half a mile before it loses itself in the lake; the natural outlet lies near present Madison Street. Lake vessels anchor half a mile offshore and lighter their cargo. The half mile has a period eyewitness behind it as of 2026-08-11: Swearingen, arriving 17 August 1803, puts the fort site 'a half mile above the mouth' and gives the reason the mouth was where it was — the river stood 'dead water, owing to its being stopped up at the mouth, by the washing of sand, from the lakes'. That is this epoch's defining condition stated by a man standing in it, and it is why it cannot be carried into e1834_harbor_cut, where the bar is cut. See docs/RESEARCH/swearingen_1803.md § 7. As of T-1242 this epoch's SHORELINE exists: shore_1812_pre_cut carries its own derived geometry with the cut and the piers absent and the mouth at Swearingen's half mile. The epoch stays `planned` because no ground has been generated from it - the terrain spec, the heightfield and the meshes are T-1243.

layer_status.shoreline: derived by tools/derive_shore_1812.py from data/terrain/1812_mouth_readings.json and the Wright 1834 trace: the pre-cut mouth, the continuous baymouth spit, the channel behind it and the lake shore south of the outlet - planform only
layer_status.river: not written - the 1812 water polygon and its banks follow the terrain spec, and both belong to T-1243
layer_status.terrain_spec: not written - T-1243 owns it, and it is where any 1812 ELEVATION has to be argued for. Nothing in the shoreline layer claims a height.

epochs.title: The harbor cut and the decaying old channel
epochs.note: The 200-ft cut through the bar is open and working, scoured by the February 1834 storm; the piers are growing into the lake; the old southward channel behind the sand tongue is silting into a backwater; fresh sand is beginning to accrete north of the north pier. Shoaling is chronic. This is the ground state for the 1835 scene.

layer_status.shoreline: not written — the 1835 lake shore runs along the modern Michigan Avenue line, about 1.4 km east of the forks quadrant; it belongs to the harbour parcel
layer_status.river: traced from Wright 1834 by tools/trace_river.py: water polygon plus one bank line per division shore
layer_status.hydrology: traced: the north-side slough, as a centreline, because its bank wash survives in only five fragments
layer_status.terrain_spec: authored zone table — every elevation cites a numbered zone in docs/research/01-terrain-hydrology.md
layer_status.heightfield: generated by generators/terrain_gen.py; ships heightfield.bin alongside, and names the ground and water GLBs the renderer loads
layer_status.extent: 640 m square centred on the datum origin. Outside it the renderer has no terrain data and says so.

epochs.title: Canal era wharfing and early fills
epochs.note: Placeholder. The Illinois and Michigan Canal opens 1848; wharfing and early filling begin to regularize the banks.

epochs.title: The city raises itself out of the mud
epochs.note: Placeholder. Chesbrough's sewerage plan sets the South Division crown at 14 ft above datum; sewers are laid above the old ground and buried under new fill; buildings are jacked 4 to 14 ft. The original 1835 ground surface disappears under the city.

epochs.title: The burnt district and the fills that followed
epochs.note: The ground state the Prairie Avenue scene stands on. The owner's ruling of 2026-09-26 centred that scene on 1904; this epoch's representative_date is still T-1249's 1 July 1888, derived in data/terrain/1880s_scene_date_constraints.json for the 1880s framing, and it stays because the owner said the 1888 records may. As of T-1250 the epoch has a SHORELINE and still no ground: shore_1880s_ic_edge carries its own traced 1904 line off Sanborn 1911 and Robinson 1886 (tools/trace_ic_edge_1904.py), and since T-1251 it has a terrain spec: street crowns at Z +12.3 to +15.1 ft over the internal datum, 2.9-5.7 ft over the conjectural 1835 surface, which the two epochs' heightfields are NOT offsets of. Since T-1738 it has a heightfield and baked ground and water meshes, and since T-1739 the 1904 scene renders them. THE 1852 TRESTLE, RULED (T-1250): this note used to say the Illinois Central trestle 'already fixed the shore in 1852'. The Chicago Public Library's history of Grant Park (cpl_grant_park_history_1830_1871) sources the 1852 trestle and refuses the sentence: the trestle stood about 300 ft east of Michigan Avenue with 'a substantial lagoon extending south to 12th street where the railroad came on shore' - water behind it north of Twelfth, which is not a fixed shore, and no trestle at all on the Prairie Avenue reach, where the railroad ran on the beach. So the claim is not restored. What the sheets show instead is that the edge beside the tracks MOVED: 17 to 20 m east between 1886 and 1911.

layer_status.shoreline: traced by tools/trace_ic_edge_1904.py (T-1250) off Sanborn 1911 sheets 20 and 28 and Robinson 1886 plate 10: the 1904 edge beside the Illinois Central, N -2900 to N -3800 - planform only, no height
layer_status.terrain_spec: authored zone table (T-1251): twelve street crowns read off the modern bare-earth model (three confirmed by standing houses of the period), graded lots, the Illinois Central embankment, the made ground of 1886-1911 and the lake shelf, every figure citing a numbered zone in docs/RESEARCH/terrain_e1871_postfire.md and re-derived by tools/check_terrain_e1871.py
layer_status.heightfield: generated by generators/terrain_gen_graded.py (T-1738) from the zone table and the scene line, 281 x 361 samples at 2.5 m, and baked to assets/gltf/terrain__e1871_postfire.glb and water__e1871_postfire.glb (mesh within 2.5 mm of the field). Rendered by data/scenes/1904.json (T-1739), the scene /4d/1904/ opens
layer_status.extent: the 1904 Prairie Avenue reach, local E +1100 to +1800 and N -3800 to -2900 (Michigan Avenue to the lake, just north of 16th Street to Cermak Road); the shoreline spans it, and T-1251's spec will state the same box

epochs.to_basis: T-1250. The interval used to close at 1900-12-31, which a 1904 scene could not stand inside. It now closes on the year of the Sanborn sheets that trace its shoreline: nothing in this epoch is asserted past the sheets that draw it.
